timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Six categories of threats. Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Info Disclosure, DoS, and Elevation of Privilege.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Can you break those down simply?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Spoofing is pretending to be someone else. Tampering is modifying data. Repudiation is denying you did something.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Info Disclosure is leaking data. DoS is crashing the system. Elevation of Privilege is gaining unauthorized access.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How do you actually apply this?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: You draw a Data Flow Diagram, identify trust boundaries, then ask STRIDE questions for each element.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Microsoft's Threat Modeling Tool automates half of it. It generates threat trees from your diagram.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It breaks down a high-level threat into the exact steps an attacker would take. Great for prioritizing.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How do you decide which threats matter most?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Risk matrix. Likelihood times impact. Focus on what's realistic and devastating.
